direction.comments: The direction on a macroscale has a warm indie feel that really complements the coming-of-age story; The direction on a microscale is executed well as it explores the growing emotions of these adolescent characters in their Catholic school world; The storytelling is pretty standard for a coming-of-age story, using empathy and relatability to drive the narrative for the audience; Tension is built by evoking feelings that the audience can empathize with, making you relate to the characters and feel their pain

performance.comments: Carries the movie well and feels like a teenager who feels lost in this world, battling his faith with his growing emotions; has pretty good chemistry with the cast
Plays the mother figure well as she has this mother-son dynamic that feels important for this story, especially with how religion is tied to it
Really feels like a natural despite playing a teenage character as she really has a control of her emotions and plays the role with a lot of poise; has pretty good chemistry with Jack Ryan

The best performance in the movie as he is perfect comedic timing and plays of Jake Ryan very well; he truly feels like a star in the making the way he is a scene-stealer, and I will be watching his career closely

cast.comments: Surprisingly good for a cast that is mostly child actors, which is a testament to the director and the talent they were able to scout; the chemistry is pretty good for the cast, especially considering it is mostly child actors

story.comments: The concept is a coming-of-age story that deals with the clash of conservative Catholic values for a teen who is coming to terms with his teenage emotions; The plot structure is your standard coming-of-age structure; The character writing is integral to the story as the juxtaposition this main character feels between his faith and his emotions is the driving force of the narrative

screenplay.comments: The dialogue is pretty good and feels natural for high schoolers in the mid-2000s; The humor is good and feels very topical for a coming-of-age story set during the mid-2000s; The symbolism is strong as the movie shows the dichotomy between the main character's faith and his growing emotions, acting as somewhat of a crisis-of-faith story layered inside of a coming-of-age story; The foreshadowing is fine

score.comments: The score helps establish the tone and feel of the movie, especially with the coming-of-age themes, and the movie has a warm indie feel

cinematography.comments: The cinematography does a good job capturing the warm indie feel of the movie as it helps make the movie feel like a coming-of-age story

editing.comments: The editing complements the cinematography well in helping establish the warm indie feel of the movie, but I am not a huge fan of the sharp cuts they use, especially in the end

review.pacing: The pacing is pretty good for the most part, though it does feel a bit slow in some places and could have been trimmed by 10-15 minutes
review.climax: The climax feels wholesome and like a natural conclusion to the story
review.tone: The tone is that of a coming-of-age story set in the mid-2000s, and they execute this very well, especially from the perspective of a child during that time period
review.final_notes: The fact that there are four Legend of Zelda references and the movie starts off by showing Wind Waker is an instant point boost from me; I was sent a screener for this movie
review.overall: Overall, 'Lemonade Blessing' is a pretty good coming-of-age story that explores the dichotomy of faith and the growing emotions of an adolescent boy going to a Catholic school, and it executes this well with its warm indie cinematography and relatable characters; while the cast as a whole exceeds expectations considering it is mostly child actors, Miles J. Harvey is a real scene-stealer with perfect comedic timing; also, the fact that this movie starts off by showing Wind Waker and has four Legend of Zelda references is an instant boost for me
